name: Veldtmark StormDrift Packable Rain Shell
description: A packable hooded rain jacket in deep teal with matte black port-aligned seams, aimed at the Tier-3 to 4 daily commuter market. Stuffs into its own chest pocket to fist-size. Rear panel has a clean spinal-rig channel sewn in as standard, and the hood has a magnetic front seal for one-hand closure in a downpour.
functionality: Packable waterproof shell with neural port alignment, spinal rig channel, and magnetic one-hand hood seal.
what_it_says: Competent, low-profile, and prepared — someone who doesn't make a production of being ready for anything.
story_hooks: The jacket's RFID tag has been clipped — it was sold outside official channels, possibly from a Veldtmark warehouse job.
Two of these jackets in identical color have shown up at different crime scenes in Circuit. Different owners, no connection found yet.

physical_description.visual_profile: Sleek, utilitarian rain shell with a modern athletic silhouette. When packed, nearly invisible—a fist-sized bundle. When worn, it drapes with minimal bulk, emphasizing clean lines and functional geometry. The deep teal reads as professional-adjacent without corporate pretension.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed athletic cut with tapered sleeves. Sits just past the hip. Designed for layering over augmentation rigs or standard wear without restriction. Packs down to eliminate storage footprint.
physical_description.primary_material: Lightweight synthetic hydrophobic weave (likely recycled polyester composite with DWR treatment). Matte finish suggests mid-tier manufacturing—durable, not luxe.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly crinkled when packed. Port-aligned seams are reinforced with micro-welded tape, creating subtle ridged lines across the torso. Hood fabric is marginally softer than body panels.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep teal (primary)—desaturated enough to read practical rather than fashion-forward. Matte black seam tape and spinal-rig channel create strong vertical accent lines down the back. Minimal contrast branding.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap hood seal (front center). Main body likely front-zip. Chest pocket features self-sealing friction fit for storage pouch.
distinctive_features: Packable into own chest pocket—stores to fist-size for commute flexibility
Rear spinal-rig channel: pre-sewn conduit for augmentation cable management, a nod to Tier-3/4 clientele with active subcutaneous or skeletal mods
Magnetic hood seal for one-handed closure during rain or quick deployment
Port-aligned matte black seams: both reinforcement and visual reference to tech integration
Minimal visible branding—Veldtmark wordmark likely small, upper chest
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 functional. Pricing suggests Φ180–280 range. Not corpo luxury, but above salvage. Built for the daily GLMZ commuter with modest augmentation.
physical_description.cultural_context: Marks the wearer as practical, transit-dependent, and likely augmented. Suggests technical literacy without wealth signaling. Common among mid-level corp workers, independent contractors, and station dock staff. The spinal-rig channel is subtle gatekeeping—you recognize it only if you have active mods.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new, but designed to weather. After 6 months: minor creasing in storage folds, possible fraying at seam edges, scuff marks on the lower torso from bag straps. Wears in gracefully rather than degrading.
